summary: Apex's memory works in resident mode: you can tell it to remember, recall or forget things by voice or chat. It loads your top 15 memories and the APEX_MEMORY/APEX_USER files at startup, consolidates them every 6 hours from the awareness heartbeat, and keeps Obsidian-style notes, a documents editor and cited research answers. The weak spots: the Memory page's own 'Save' form is broken (HTTP 422). Start-Apex-Platform.cmd forces Hugging Face offline mode, and nothing pre-downloads the embedding model, so the Knowledge base and semantic recall can quietly drop to keyword matching. Some background jobs (skill curator, Time Capsule log) are wired only in main.py, not in resident mode. The research-grade 'governed memory' layer is API-only and no normal turn ever uses it.

features.name: Long-term memory (remember / recall / forget)
features.what: Apex saves facts, preferences, decisions and projects to a SQLite database (~/.voice_agent_memory.db) and finds them again by meaning, using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, or by keywords when the embedding model is missing.
features.how_to_use: Automatic, and on request: say or type 'remember that...', 'what do you know about...', 'forget memory #12'. The model calls the remember/recall/forget tools.

gaps.issue: The Memory page's 'Remember something' Save button always fails with HTTP 422. scoped-memory.js passes body: JSON.stringify({...}) to app.js api(), which stringifies it a second time, so the server gets a JSON string instead of an object. The page check stubs api() with a fake that expects a string, so it passes while the real page fails.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/static/scoped-memory.js:36; dashboard/static/app.js:72-80 (body: JSON.stringify(opts.body)); dashboard/server.py:434-444 (payload: dict); scripts/check_scoped_memory_ui.cjs:7 (JSON.parse(options.body) encodes the wrong contract)
gaps.fix_hint: In scoped-memory.js pass body:{content:...,kind:...} (a plain object) like every other caller in app.js. Change the check's api stub to receive an object, so the double-encode would fail it.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read app.js api() and confirmed it is the global api (team.js's api is IIFE-scoped). Ran a FastAPI TestClient snippet with an identical 'payload: dict' route and a double-JSON-encoded body: 422 'Input should be a valid dictionary'. Ran node: JSON.stringify of the stringified object yields a quoted string.

gaps.issue: Start-Apex-Platform.cmd sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 / TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 for Apex, and nothing in the repo pre-downloads the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model. If it was never cached on the laptop, the Knowledge base refuses to index or search ('Embedding model unavailable... check internet', which is misleading because internet is not the problem). Memory recall and vault search drop to keyword matching, new memories get no embedding, and entity fuzzy-merge is off. All of this is quiet except one console line.
gaps.evidence: scripts/run_apex_platform.py:121,143-146,187; agent/longterm.py:44-51 (SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2'), failure is cached as False for the process); agent/knowledge.py:72-74,135-137; no other reference to MiniLM in scripts/ or setup .cmd files
gaps.fix_hint: Download the model during setup (Apex.bat or a Setup step) or in Test-Apex-Hardware. Or exempt it from offline mode / point SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS_HOME at a bundled copy. Show 'embedding model missing' on the Memory/Knowledge pages.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the launcher (sets the env vars and passes apex_env to run_apex_qwen.py --resident) and grepped the whole repo for MiniLM/model download. Only longterm.py loads it, and lazily. Not run on Windows: if the laptop ever ran Start-Apex-All.cmd (no offline flag) and used memory, the model may already be cached.

gaps.issue: The Knowledge base never removes files you delete or move. Reindex only adds or updates, and the 'removed' counter is hard-coded to 0, so search keeps returning chunks of files that no longer exist.
gaps.evidence: agent/knowledge.py:75-78 (deleted = 0, never incremented), 101-126; remove_path() (128-132) has no caller in the repo
gaps.fix_hint: At the end of reindex(), delete kb_chunks rows whose path is under the reindexed roots but no longer exists, and count them in 'removed'. Add a test.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran a scratchpad snippet with a temp DB and a fake embedding model: indexed a folder, deleted the file, reindexed ('0 removed'). stats() still showed 1 file and search('hello') still returned a.md.

gaps.issue: The skill curator (weekly archive/dedup of stale skills) is started only by main.py. Resident mode, the owner's only launcher, never runs it, and no dashboard page calls /api/curator/*.
gaps.evidence: main.py:358-375; app/resident.py has no 'curator' reference; dashboard/server.py:2656-2685; no dashboard/static file references api/curator
gaps.fix_hint: Move the curator tick into a shared helper started from both main.py and app/resident.py (as schema.init_all and build_monitor were). Add a button on the Skills tab.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep -rn curator app/ and agent/*.py (only telemetry's call-site name) and dashboard/static: no hits besides main.py and the routes.

gaps.issue: In resident mode the Time Capsule panel's log is always empty: app/resident.py never calls dash.set_timecapsule(), so /api/timecapsule returns log=[] even though the capsule is capturing and speaking. The Guardian log has the same omission.
gaps.evidence: main.py:415-418 (set_guardian/set_timecapsule); app/resident.py:271-288 (only set_agent and attach_live_feed); dashboard/server.py:1063-1067 (log=[] when _timecapsule_ref is None)
gaps.fix_hint: In app/resident.py, after dash.set_agent, call dash.set_guardian(awareness_monitor.guardian) and dash.set_timecapsule(awareness_monitor.timecapsule) when present. Better: move it into awareness.attach_live_feed.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep 'set_timecapsule|set_guardian' app/resident.py found nothing; read server.py lines 1054-1076. The toggle still works because tick() reads config each time (agent/timecapsule.py:218).

gaps.issue: Reflection auto-applies its own suggestions when it rates them 85%+ confident, including 'forget' and 'supersedes_id' actions that hard-DELETE your memories. No approval, no trash, no undo. MEMORY_WRITE_APPROVAL does not cover this path.
gaps.evidence: agent/reflection.py:144 (prompt offers {type: forget}), 328-347 (auto-apply at config.REFLECTION_AUTO_APPLY_THRESHOLD=0.85, config.py:317), 477-492; agent/longterm.py:486-489 (DELETE FROM memories)
gaps.fix_hint: Never auto-apply forget/supersede: keep them pending for review. Or soft-delete (status column) with an undo on the Reflections tab.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the prompt, the auto-apply loop and _apply_action. grep MEMORY_WRITE_APPROVAL: only longterm.save_memory_entry (longterm.py:600) and vault.py:106 check it.

gaps.issue: Picking a model on the dashboard (for example deepseek-flash) changes only the chat model. config.AGENT_MODEL and BACKGROUND_MODEL keep the .env value (default claude-opus-5). Memory consolidation, summarization, profile digest, Time Capsule extraction and the Documents AI-edit then still call that model, and fail quietly if there is no Anthropic key.
gaps.evidence: dashboard/server.py:410-423 -> agent/core.py:3665 (sets self._model only); config.py:21,25-31; agent/telemetry.py:196-209 (background sites use config.BACKGROUND_MODEL); agent/documents.py:152
gaps.fix_hint: Either persist the chosen model as AGENT_MODEL/BACKGROUND_MODEL, or show on the Models page which model background memory jobs use. Ask the owner to set AGENT_MODEL=deepseek-flash in .env.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read set_model and the /api/model route (no config/.env write), config defaults and telemetry._resolve_call. Impact depends on the owner's .env, which I cannot see.

gaps.issue: No direct tests for the Knowledge base (knowledge.reindex/search), the entity graph (agent/entities.py), curator.run, the apex_note tool or the /api/timecapsule route.
gaps.evidence: grep of tests/: knowledge only appears as tool names (tests/test_subagent_scope.py:24, tests/test_apocalypse.py:79); entities only via tests/test_reflection.py digest shape
gaps.fix_hint: Add small tests with a fake embedder (as in the snippet used for the KB gap).
gaps.how_confirmed: grep -rl for knowledge.search/reindex, upsert_entity, curator, apex_note, api/timecapsule in tests/

gaps.issue: Knowledge base search loads every chunk and embedding from SQLite on every query (no cap, no vector index), so a big folder (say D: library notes) will make kb_search slow.
gaps.fix_hint: Cap candidates like longterm._RECALL_CANDIDATE_CAP, or cache vectors in memory.

gaps.issue: Facts flushed by the summarizer are saved with kind='conversation', which remember() silently rewrites to 'note'. They are never de-duplicated, so the same fact can pile up at importance 6.
gaps.fix_hint: Use kind='fact' and skip near-duplicates (cosine > 0.9) before inserting.

gaps.issue: Resident mode skips vault.init_vault(), so the vault README is never written and old ~/.apex/memory files are never migrated. Folders still appear because every writer calls _ensure(). It also skips main.py's 'Nightly reflection' scheduled task, which is harmless because the awareness heartbeat runs consolidation every 6h.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep init_vault/Nightly reflection in app/resident.py: none.

gaps.issue: AgentCore.run(memory_context=...) is never passed by any caller, so the governed-memory scope is never active in normal turns. Its 'Approved evidence panel' messages in remember/recall/forget are dead branches for the owner.
gaps.evidence: agent/core.py:3936,3970; agent/core.py:2976-3007; grep memory_context finds only the definition
gaps.fix_hint: Either wire it to a real page or label the module experimental in docs.
gaps.how_confirmed: grep -rn memory_context across agent/ dashboard/ app/ main.py

needs_from_owner: On the laptop, check whether the embedding model is cached: look for a folder named models--sentence-transformers--all-MiniLM-L6-v2 under C:\Users\alexk\.cache\huggingface\hub. If it is missing, run Start-Apex-All.cmd once with internet and say 'remember that test' so it downloads (about 90 MB), then go back to Start-Apex-Platform.cmd.
Tell us whether .env sets AGENT_MODEL=deepseek-flash, or whether you only pick DeepSeek on the dashboard. If the latter, background memory jobs still try Claude.
After the UTF-8 fix, open the Memory tab and try the Save form (expected to fail with HTTP 422 until fixed). Telling Apex 'remember ...' by voice works instead.
Decide whether reflection may delete memories on its own (today it can, at 85% confidence).
Decide where the vault should live (VAULT_PATH; default C:\Users\alexk\Documents\Apex). If Documents is redirected to OneDrive, Obsidian may look elsewhere.
Press Reindex on the Knowledge base tab with the folders you want searchable. Nothing is indexed until you do.

rating.why: The core memory, reflection, vault search, documents and cited answers are real, wired in resident mode and well tested. But the Memory page Save is broken, embeddings may be missing under the Platform launcher, the KB keeps deleted files, and several pieces are main.py-only or experimental.
